title: position field table is stale — omits value 7 (Outlet) and outletName
reality: packages/shared/src/schemas/lorebook.schema.ts:180-187 refines position to accept 0, 1, 2, OR 7, with the validation message 'Position must be Before, After, At Depth, or Outlet', plus a sibling outletName field (trimmed string, max 200, default ''). references/lorebooks.md line 50 documents position as '0, 1, or 2' and never mentions Outlet or outletName.
fix: Update the position row in the entry-field table of references/lorebooks.md to 0/1/2/7 and add an outletName row. Then document the Outlet mechanism: an Outlet entry is placed wherever {{outlet::name}} appears in the prompt, with CASE-SENSITIVE name matching. This is a genuine factual error in a schema table, and it hides the engine's most precise content-placement feature.

title: activationConditions operator set not enumerated
reality: activationConditionSchema (lorebook.schema.ts:38-42) defines operator as z.enum(['equals','not_equals','contains','not_contains','gt','lt']) over a {field, operator, value} triple. references/lorebooks.md line 65 describes activationConditions as 'Game-state gates (field, operator, value)' without listing the six operators.
fix: List the six operators in the activationConditions row of references/lorebooks.md. Without them the field is undocumented in practice — a user cannot author a condition from the current description.

title: lorebookFilterModeSchema (any/include/exclude) not documented
reality: lorebook.schema.ts:25 defines lorebookFilterModeSchema = z.enum(['any','include','exclude']), the filter mode paired with the matching-source list. references/lorebooks.md documents additionalMatchingSources but not the mode governing how they filter.
fix: Add the filter mode to the additionalMatchingSources row in references/lorebooks.md. include vs exclude vs any changes activation semantics substantially and is currently invisible.

title: Entry role field (system/user/assistant) coverage unverified
reality: lorebook.schema.ts defines role: z.enum(['system','user','assistant']).default('system') on the entry, controlling which message role the injected content is attributed to.
fix: Confirm whether references/lorebooks.md's field table carries `role`; if not, add it with the default. Role attribution materially affects how strongly a model weighs injected lore, which is directly relevant to the skill's prompt-design advice.
